China’s Export Engine Meets Europe’s Carbon Rules

AJ Cortese

Gavekal Technologies: New Energy | 3 Aug 2026

Europe’s desire to limit imports of carbon-intensive goods is leading to changes in industrial China. Beijing has launched a set of zero-carbon industrial parks that will tightly link factories with renewable energy sources, helping them cut their carbon footprint and comply with new EU regulations that will tax carbon-intensive steel and aluminum imports and bar entry to batteries that fail to meet carbon limits. In the longer run, zero-carbon parks could create another opportunity. Plenty of industries in emerging markets suffer from power outages and inefficient electricity management.
